stories.h: Johnny Depp's Scrooge sinks Ti West's Ebenezer
sum: Screen's Nikki Baughan finds Ti West's take on A Christmas Carol surprisingly safe. Despite a horror director in charge, the Paramount release plays as yet another faithful retelling, and Johnny Depp's Scrooge is more cartoon than character. The film leans so hard on his star wattage that everything else becomes decoration.

There are bright spots: Ian McKellen and Rupert Grint bring warmth, Andrea Riseborough and Tramell Tillman stand out, and the ghost effects and production design impress. West slips in a few genuinely scary gothic moments, but the film is too intense for small children and too tame for adults, landing in a forgettable middle.
pts: Rolling out globally from 11 Nov via Paramount
Depp's lead called a caricature; supporting cast praised
Verdict: underwhelming and unnecessary

stories.h: Fjord: Mungiu's Norway drama gets a savage notice
sum: Cristian Mungiu's new film stars Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve as a Romanian-Norwegian couple raising five children under a strict Christian regime on a remote stretch of Norwegian coast. When a teacher spots bruises on their eldest daughter, child services step in, the children are removed and the parents face possible prison.

Little White Lies' David Jenkins is scathing, as the blunt headline makes plain. His main complaint is that the film never makes clear whether the parents did anything wrong, so the drama turns into a study of their suffering rather than a real moral puzzle. It runs 146 minutes and opens on 13 November.
pts: Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve star
Opens 13 Nov; 146 minutes
LWLies: ducks its own central question

stories.h: Being Heumann: likeable, conventional activist biopic
sum: CODA director Siân Heder tells the story of disability rights campaigner Judy Heumann, who in 1977 led a San Francisco sit-in pushing the US government to enforce Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act. Ruth Madeley plays Heumann, with Dylan O'Brien as a reporter drawn into the cause and Mark Ruffalo as the official avoiding her calls.

LWLies calls it warm and important but formally safe, a familiar triumph-over-adversity story whose politics are often softened. Madeley's fiery, charismatic lead does most of the heavy lifting, and the ensemble of disabled actors is a real plus. It opens 13 November and is streaming on Apple TV+.
pts: Ruth Madeley's lead performance is the highlight
Feel-good in the CODA mould
In select cinemas and on Apple TV+

stories.h: Under The Judas Tree: absorbing Greek crime debut
sum: Premiering at Thessaloniki, Christos Houliaras's first fiction feature follows Elias, a man fleeing failures in Athens who returns to his mountain village. Staying with an old policeman friend, he becomes fixated on an unidentified young woman found dead in the woods, and starts investigating when the police seem uninterested.

Screen's Boyd van Hoeij calls it a small, precision-built character study whose tension tightens as the pieces fall into place. Muted colours and overcast landscapes give it a bleak, uneasy mood, and Alexis Kalofolias is a magnetic lead. The only flaw is repeated visions of the victim that overstate things. Marni Films handles sales.
pts: World premiere at Thessaloniki
Slow-burn village mystery with strong visuals
Tipped for festivals and crime-hungry streamers

stories.h: UK-Ireland box office has its best year since the pandemic
sum: With eight weeks still to go, 2026 cinema takings in the UK and Ireland have hit £1.07bn, already beating every full year since 2020. The year is running 22% ahead of 2025 at the same point, and October alone was up 35%, led by Colleen Hoover adaptation Verity with £11.8m.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day leads the year with £100.3m, ahead of The Odyssey and Toy Story 5. A busy run of releases, including Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend, Ebenezer and the new Hunger Games, could push the total towards 2019's pre-pandemic £1.35bn.
pts: £1.07bn so far, beating 2021–2025 totals
Spider-Man: Brand New Day tops the year at £100.3m
Holiday slate could close gap to 2019

stories.h: Lionsgate buys Alma Har'el's high-seas caper Wet
stories.why: Early buzz on a starry indie
sum: Lionsgate has taken North American and UK rights to Wet, the next film from Honey Boy director Alma Har'el. The cast is stacked: Connor Storrie of Heated Rivalry, Rebecca Ferguson, Odessa A'zion, Javier Bardem, singer Rosalía and Lukas Haas.

Plot details are under wraps beyond a tagline billing it as a caper on the high seas. Har'el co-wrote the script with Christian Stangeby, Fifth Season and 193 are producing, and shooting starts in the Dominican Republic in 2027.
pts: Rosalía and Javier Bardem in the cast
Lionsgate takes North America and UK
Shoots in the Dominican Republic in 2027

stories.h: Sundance courts Gen Z for its first Colorado edition
stories.why: Big shift for indie film's top fest
sum: Sundance's first edition in Boulder, Colorado, running 21–31 January 2027, will actively court the city's roughly 36,000 university students, CEO David Linde told an AFM panel. The festival is working to make screenings easier for students to get into, hoping for a livelier atmosphere.

Panellists said young audiences are now what every distributor wants, after Gen Z powered summer hits like Backrooms. About 60% of the 2026 lineup found distribution, and a new Academy rule makes the World Cinema grand jury winner eligible for the international Oscar. Sundance will publish an AI policy within a month.
pts: Boulder edition runs 21–31 Jan 2027
Students targeted with easier access
AI policy statement coming within a month

stories.h: Krieps, Bang and Haigh join Cotillard's Marrakech jury
stories.why: Key showcase for new world cinema
sum: The 23rd Marrakech International Film Festival has named its nine-member jury under president Marion Cotillard. Joining her are Vicky Krieps, Claes Bang, All of Us Strangers director Andrew Haigh, Oscar-nominated Tunisian filmmaker Kaouther Ben Hania, Emma Mackey and Gilles Lellouche.

Ramata-Toulaye Sy and Moroccan director-producer Saïd Hamich Benlarbi complete the panel. They will award the Étoile d'Or to one of 14 first or second features in competition. The festival runs 20–28 November, with winners announced at the closing night.
pts: Marion Cotillard is jury president
14 debut and second features compete
Festival runs 20–28 Nov

stories.h: Don Hertzfeldt on Paper Trail, a life told in paper scraps
sum: Letterboxd talks at length with animator Don Hertzfeldt about Paper Trail, a 14-minute short that traces one man's life entirely through paper: crayon drawings, homework, letters, job applications and office memos. It won a special jury prize at Sundance and the top prize at Annecy, and is now free to watch as a Vimeo Staff Pick Premiere.

Hertzfeldt discusses animators' odd relationship with time, why stick figures leave room for viewers' own feelings, influences such as Koyaanisqatsi and Powers of Ten, and why he still edits in ancient software. He also argues that push-button AI filmmaking strips out the struggle that makes art matter.
pts: Paper Trail is free on Vimeo now
Won the Annecy Crystal, a first for a US film in 22 years
It's Such a Beautiful Day is on Letterboxd Video Store

stories.h: Letterboxd's five under-the-radar picks for November
sum: Letterboxd's monthly Watchlist This! rounds up five films bubbling under the mainstream. Highlights include Victorian Psycho, a gothic horror satire with Maika Monroe as a governess with dark urges, and Paul Thomas Anderson's concert film of Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall.

Also picked: Marie Kreutzer's Gentle Monster, with Léa Seydoux as a pianist whose husband faces a disturbing investigation, streaming on Netflix from 18 November; Andrey Zvyagintsev's Russian thriller Minotaur, from MUBI; and Being Heumann, already on Apple TV+.
pts: Gentle Monster hits Netflix 18 Nov
Being Heumann streaming on Apple TV+
New Zvyagintsev and PTA titles included

stories.h: Nothing new from Beyoncé or Kendrick Lamar today
sum: No releases, tour dates, features or announcements in the last 24 hours.

stories.h: Krill return with Secret Language, Stereogum's Album of the Week
sum: Boston indie-rock cult heroes Krill release Secret Language today on Exploding In Sound, their first album in more than ten years. Stereogum made it Album of the Week ahead of release, and premiered the title track as the final single after "Commemorative Plaque," "Dominate" and "Hawaii."

Songwriter Jonah Furman says the title song is about family life: its opening verses come from reading Goodnight Moon backwards, a bedtime game his kids dislike, and it ends with the children asleep as he tries to describe being in love inside a marriage. Fran's Maria Jacobson sings backing vocals and Macie Stewart plays violin.
pts: First Krill album in over a decade, out Nov 13
Stereogum Album of the Week
Title track features Macie Stewart on violin

stories.h: Stereogum's 40 best new artists of 2026
sum: Stereogum's annual fall roundup picks 40 emerging acts who made a big leap this year, most on a first album or without one yet. It is alphabetical rather than ranked, and each entry gets a short write-up plus streaming links, with Spotify and Apple Music playlists at the end.

The range is wide: indie rock, hardcore, metal, electronic, rap and pop. Names include Québécois masked math-rock duo Angine de Poitrine, Leeds dance-noise quartet Bathing Suits, Southern California project 16 Underground, Columbia signee earthsignchels, Ninja Tune trio Ebbb from the Windmill scene and London duo Worldpeace DMT.
pts: 40 acts, alphabetical, with playlists
Heavy on indie, noise and math-rock
Good for discovering next year's favourites

stories.h: Emma Ogier's debut Fly 1111 dodges the Americana box
sum: Houston-born, Nashville-based songwriter Emma Ogier mixes Texas twang, fingerpicked guitar and lo-fi vocals with sudden hard-rock swerves on her first album. The diary-like lyrics invite comparisons to Phoebe Bridgers, MJ Lenderman and Waxahatchee without sounding like copies.

Highlights are the direct opener "All These Dreams," the hooky "Baby Don't Hurt Me," the Eden Joel duet "Rocksteady/HeavyMetal" and the Zeppelin-heavy "W2F." A couple of tracks feel murky or formulaic, but the reviewer likes how restless she is and is excited to hear what she does next.
pts: Folk-rock debut with loud guitar turns
Fans of Waxahatchee and MJ Lenderman
Standout: "W2F"

stories.h: U2 praise Fontaines D.C., Geese and Lambrini Girls as new album lands
sum: U2's Carnaval De Luz, their first album in nine years, is out today on Island. In NME interviews, the Edge said he envies Lambrini Girls' sound and admires Geese and Cameron Winter's solo work, while Bono praised Winter's stage presence and said Fontaines D.C. push their peers to raise their game.

The album includes "Torn," a duet carrying Dolly Parton's final recording, and Bono wrote a song about Rosalía, who recently featured on Fontaines' "Where Is Gone?" The band also played a small BBC show at London's Tate Modern, and Stereogum calls "The Greatest Show On Earth" the best single so far.
pts: Carnaval De Luz out Nov 13
Big compliments for Fontaines D.C. and Geese
Includes Dolly Parton's final recording

stories.h: Mass Text announce Perfect New Knife, share droning "Pink Slips"
sum: Chicago collective Mass Text, led by Meat Wave frontman Chris Sutter, will release Perfect New Knife on January 29 via Solid Brass. Dehd's Jason Balla produced it, and the nine tracks include "Nice Dream 2" and "Weightlifting."

Lead single "Pink Slips" is ominous, droning post-punk that Stereogum compares to Liars, with an eerie nod to a Partridge Family hit. It grew from a home demo, keeps many original takes and uses feedback from old walkie-talkies. Release shows follow in Chicago, Minneapolis and Milwaukee in February.
pts: Album due Jan 29 on Solid Brass
Produced by Dehd's Jason Balla
Post-punk in a Liars vein

stories.h: Weird Nightmare drop power-pop single "Buzzing In My Head"
sum: Weird Nightmare, the power-pop project of former METZ frontman Alex Edkins, has a new standalone single out on Sub Pop. Stereogum praises its energetic riff, yelping lovelorn vocals and bright, glowing chorus harmonies, and notes that some of the project's best songs live outside its albums.

Holy Fuck's Graham Walsh, Edkins' partner in Noble Rot, produced it, with the Hoopla rhythm section back on drums and bass. Edkins says it's about a person, place or memory that won't leave your head. A short run of shows follows from November 18 to 22.
pts: Ex-METZ frontman's power-pop project
Out now on Sub Pop
Produced by Holy Fuck's Graham Walsh
stories.q: Weird Nightmare Buzzing In My Head

stories.h: Karen O shares solo ballad as Rapaport "discovers" Yeah Yeah Yeahs
stories.why: Indie rock icons back in focus
sum: Michael Rapaport went viral after an Instagram video hailing "Maps" as if it were by an exciting new band, apparently unaware the song came out in 2003. Stereogum notes it already went viral on TikTok in 2024 and was recently named the best rock song of the century so far by Rolling Stone.

Meanwhile Karen O has a sparse new solo song, "Soft Machine," from Space Cadet, a dialogue-free animated film based on Kid Koala's graphic novel about an astronaut's first solo mission. The film opens this weekend. YYYs also put out a Royal Albert Hall live album in September.
pts: New Karen O song "Soft Machine"
Space Cadet film opens this weekend
"Maps" keeps finding new fans

stories.h: akupergi turn urban burnout into post-punk protest
sum: Jakarta band akupergi's new single ".lampu//Kota;Mati" is a protest song about ordinary city workers rather than elites: routines, unstable pay, money stress and exhaustion. Singer Hanung draws on his own life as a worker who sometimes skips meals to save money.

Musically it mixes post-punk and post-hardcore, shaped by Molchat Doma-style coldwave and early Jimmy Eat World, while new drummer Daffa, on his first release with the band, brings dub, slow disco and Helmet-style heaviness. The band hopes to play more Jakarta venues and collectives such as Fengshui and Pokta.
pts: Jakarta post-punk/post-hardcore
About urban workers' struggles
New drummer Daffa's debut with the band

stories.h: Subang folk-rockers Nalara gather eight years on debut album Bias
sum: Nalara, a seven-piece folk-rock band from Subang, have released Bias, a nine-song album collecting their journey since forming in 2018 as Musik Hari Ini. They survived a pulled debut EP and a two-year hiatus, then renamed themselves because the old name was too generic to register.

The record mixes reworked older songs with new ones like "Sendu Membuka Mata," pairing folklore-inspired lyrics with distorted guitars, layered harmonies and fuller keys. It opens with a dark, reverb-soaked instrumental and was mastered in Nashville. Next, the band hopes to play Jakarta festivals.
pts: Nine-track folk-rock album, out since Oct 23
Distorted guitars plus folklore lyrics
Band hopes to reach Jakarta stages

stories.h: Pokémon x Crocs drop Pikachu, Gengar and Jigglypuff clogs
stories.why: Colorful, whimsical, easy to wear casually
sum: Crocs is marking Pokémon's 30th anniversary with a three-pair capsule. Pikachu gets a bright yellow Classic Clog, Gengar a deep purple one, and Jigglypuff a pastel pink Classic Platform Clog. Each keeps the usual light foam and vented toe, with character details layered on.

The pairs land on November 17 at crocs.com. Japanese pricing is about ¥13,200 for the two Classic Clogs and ¥13,750 for the platform, so international prices should come in close to standard collab-Croc money. It's the most openly playful drop of the week.
pts: Pikachu yellow, Gengar purple, Jigglypuff pink platform
Out November 17 on crocs.com
Around ¥13,200–13,750 in Japan

stories.h: HOKA and Marni bring back the Clifton, now in orange
stories.why: Bright, quirky runner for casual fits
sum: HOKA and Marni have teamed up again after their 2025 debut, this time on the Clifton 11 daily runner. It comes in Orange, White and Black, with raised 3D silicone prints, reflective hits and a plaid sockliner. Two spare sets of laces come in the box.

Underneath, it's the normal Clifton: engineered mesh, a cushy EVA midsole and HOKA's rocker shape. It's on Marni's site now and widens to HOKA and selected stores from November 13. The campaign is called Every Day Is a Marathon.
pts: Orange colorway is the standout
Wider release on HOKA from November 13
Comes with two extra sets of laces

stories.h: ASICS x JUNTAE KIM: a sneaker with detachable dried-flower hardware
stories.why: Niche Korean designer, a weird and fun sneaker
sum: Seoul designer JUNTAE KIM's first ASICS shoe is the GEL-KINETIC FR, part dress shoe and part runner. The idea is decaying flowers: gradient color fades across the upper and the ASICS stripes, the way petals dry and lose color. Real and synthetic leathers sit on ASICS running tooling.

The odd extra is clip-on floral hardware shaped like withered petals and stamens. Leave it on for a dressed-up look, take it off for everyday wear. It comes in Black, Navy and Red and goes on sale November 20 at ASICS and selected stores.
pts: Black, Navy and Red with fade effects
Removable petal-shaped hardware
Releases November 20

stories.h: Tyler, the Creator cuts the Converse Bronco Boot down to a low
stories.why: Chunky tomboy shoe from a playful label
sum: GOLF le FLEUR* and Converse have made a low-top Bronco Boot for the 1908 line. It's based on Converse's 1990s Mud Chunk, a cross between sneaker and boot. Uppers are suede and leather, with a molded rubber toe cap, a lugged sole, woven round laces and a le FLEUR* lace jewel.
Colors are Cocoa Brown, New Wheat, Eden green and Black. It's out now on the Converse and GOLF le FLEUR* sites and at selected stores. The article didn't list a price.
pts: Four colors, including Eden green
Chunky lug sole and rubber toe cap
Available now

stories.h: A$AP Rocky's worn-in PUMA Suede '94 nods to '90s skate
sum: A$AP Rocky's newest PUMA capsule is a Suede '94 in washed, distressed navy, built on an original Suede colorway. Details include a raw-edged padded tongue, a gum sole, custom branding and a gold metal lace keeper.
A matching PUMA No. 1 logo tee and hoodie complete the set, which leans on '90s skate and hip-hop. It's out now on PUMA's US site and at selected stores. No price was given.
pts: Distressed navy suede with a gum sole
Matching tee and hoodie
Out now on PUMA

stories.h: Drama Call's star-covered adidas ClimaCool 1 GTX
stories.why: Niche label, stars and pops of lime
sum: Manchester streetwear label Drama Call is on its fourth adidas project, a ClimaCool 1 GTX. It's mostly black ripstop with a GORE-TEX lining and lime trim, plus a marbled camo sole in lime, black and grey. Big halftone stars on the insoles and silver stars on the heel add the playful part.
It launches November 14 on Drama Call's own site, then on the adidas CONFIRMED app and at selected stores from November 15. Price is still to be confirmed. Rapper Suggz fronts the campaign.
pts: Black with lime accents and camo sole
Drama Call site Nov 14, CONFIRMED Nov 15
Waterproof GORE-TEX build

stories.h: This week's drops: Metallica x MADSAKI, Palace, BBC x Pokémon
stories.why: Rock graphics and playful capsules in one list
sum: Hypebeast's weekly list has eight releases. The rock picks are a second Metallica x MADSAKI capsule, with redrawn band graphics on jackets and knits (November 14 via PARADISE TOKYO), and a Supreme capsule with the Elliott Smith estate. For color, there's Palace Winter Drop 7 outerwear, including a balaclava puffer.

Also on the list: a Billionaire Boys Club x Pokémon 30th-anniversary capsule, Kith's Knicks collection, LOEWE's Nightmare Before Christmas line, Oakley x Metalwood, and Kaptain Sunshine x COVERCHORD. Most drop between November 12 and 14, and Asia often gets them a day later.
pts: Metallica x MADSAKI drops November 14
Palace and BBC x Pokémon bring color
Most drops land Nov 12–14

stories.h: Simone Rocha and Crocs end their run with pearl ballet clogs
sum: Simone Rocha's sixth and final Crocs drop has three shoes. The Ballerina Platform has pointe-shoe molding, ribbon embossing, bows, pearls and crystals. There's also a shearling-lined Classic Clog and a trail-style Quick Trail Racer with decorative extras. The palette is mostly neutral: latte, khaki, coffee and black.

Fumi Imano shot the campaign in Tokyo. Everything goes on sale worldwide November 17 through Crocs, Simone Rocha and selected stores. As the last chapter of a well-loved collab, it may sell out quickly.
pts: Final Simone Rocha x Crocs drop
Three styles, from ballet to trail
Out globally November 17

stories.h: What people wore to Pouffe, London's silly queer rave
stories.why: Playful, DIY club style for inspiration
sum: Dazed photographed the second Pouffe night, a queer rave in Tottenham hosted by William Craven, Jam and Billy at Unit 58. There's no dress code. The hosts just want people to come as their freest selves, and the mood is sexy but goofy.

Dancewear was everywhere: sporty shorts, cropped vests, lace mesh and studded bras. Standout looks paired marbled vintage furs with printed silk slips, and one person wore a Carmela Soprano tee. Cameron Hendry took the photos.
pts: Sporty shorts and cropped vests dominated
Vintage fur over silk slips
Joke tees as statement pieces

stories.h: Gibran resigns as vice president over diploma ruling
stories.why: Dynasty politics cracks at the top
sum: Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, eldest son of former president Joko Widodo, handed his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto and parliament on Thursday, two years into his five-year term. Prabowo said he accepted it reluctantly. Last month the Constitutional Court and Supreme Court found that the documents Gibran filed on his overseas schooling did not meet election requirements; critics say he never earned a high school diploma.

A day earlier, 120 lawmakers from eight parties had filed a motion that could lead to impeachment. The vacancy does not trigger an election: the MPR must pick a replacement from two presidential nominees within 60 days. Al Jazeera notes weeks of street protests over living costs, corruption, authoritarianism and the wildfire response.
pts: Resignation follows court rulings against his education documents
120 DPR members had already launched an impeachment motion
MPR picks a successor from two Prabowo nominees within 60 days

stories.h: 154 arrested as Yogyakarta Heroes Day protest is crushed
sum: Protesters gathered on 10 November at Titik Nol, the DIY regional parliament and Tugu, demanding troops return to barracks, investigations into shootings in Aceh and Papua, a national disaster declaration for the forest fires and lower taxes. Police say about 100 people attacked the DPRD building with firecrackers, Molotovs and stones; by the next morning they reported 154 arrests, including minors.

LBH Yogyakarta says police skipped required de-escalation steps, that plainclothes officers made arrests, and that 13 people were unaccounted for. It reported two injured at hospital, one with a head wound. Student press accounts say police fired tear gas toward UGM, which police deny. UGM's social sciences faculty demanded the students' release.
pts: Police count rose from 104 to 154 detained, including children
LBH alleges excessive force and missing detainees
Campus accounts contradict police on tear gas at UGM

stories.h: Land seized by army-led task force keeps burning
stories.why: Military land grab meets haze crisis
sum: A joint investigation by Project Multatuli and IndonesiaLeaks found that at least 26 concessions seized by the military-dominated forest task force Satgas PKH burned between January 2025 and September 2026. Of roughly 6.2 million hectares seized, about 68% went to state firm Agrinas Palma, largely for palm oil, and only 18% to the forestry ministry for restoration. Greenpeace counted over 5,000 hectares burned in eight concessions in mid-2026.

Agrinas's annual report never mentions fires or peat, names few of its partner companies, and lists palm oil sales with undisclosed buyers. The task force says the recipients are responsible; Agrinas did not respond. Environmental groups call it state neglect and want tougher penalties in the forestry law revision.
pts: About 4.2 million ha of seized land handed to military-linked Agrinas
Fires hit concessions tied to Wilmar, Musim Mas, Salim and others
Agrinas and the task force publish almost no data

stories.h: Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital kills Gaza surgeon
stories.why: Ceasefire in name only in Gaza
sum: An Israeli strike hit the surgery department of Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis early Thursday, killing at least six people including surgeon Dr Rizq Abu Shuaira and a child, according to Gaza health officials, who called it a crime. Al Jazeera says it was the seventh attack on the hospital, which serves about half a million people. The Israeli military said it was targeting a Hamas commander.

The report lays out the wider toll: health authorities say 17 of Gaza's 37 hospitals are out of service and 44% of essential medicines are out of stock. Israel's Supreme Court this week refused to release detained hospital director Dr Husam Abu Safia, held for over 500 days.
pts: At least six killed, per Gaza health ministry
Seventh attack on Nasser, despite the October 2025 ceasefire
Israeli court rejects release of Dr Husam Abu Safia

stories.h: Hebron families return to looted homes after siege
stories.why: Collective punishment in the West Bank
sum: Between 23 October and 2 November, Israeli forces displaced at least 619 families, nearly 4,000 people, from two Hebron neighbourhoods after a Palestinian gunman killed two soldiers, +972 reports. The army said it was dismantling militant infrastructure; the magazine notes only four weapons were seized and calls the operation collective punishment.

Residents describe missing gold, cash and appliances, homes used as army posts, and car dealers losing hundreds of vehicles. Some homes were demolished and peaceful protests demanding return were met with force. The army says it ordered troops to protect property, found no damage claims and will investigate specific allegations.
pts: Around 4,000 people displaced for over a week
Residents report theft of cash, gold and vehicles
Army denies wrongdoing but promises to check claims

stories.h: Going home to Gaza via Rafah means risking arrest
sum: Since the Rafah crossing reopened in February, about 7,900 Palestinians have left Gaza and some 7,500 have returned, according to the EU border mission, but it opens only around three days a week and closes without warning. Israeli forces have arrested 11 returnees at the crossing, six in October, including a 60-year-old cancer patient and her daughter, whose family says they are held in Ashkelon.

Returnees may bring only one 20kg suitcase, deterring people whose livelihoods depend on laptops. Gaza's media office says over 3,000 patients have been evacuated for treatment while more than 21,000 remain on waiting lists, and accuses Israel of delays and arbitrary arrests. Israel has not explained the detentions.
pts: 11 returnees arrested at Rafah since February
Crossing opens erratically; luggage capped at 20kg
Over 21,000 patients still waiting for medical evacuation

stories.h: Israeli troops kill 14-year-old boy near Nablus
stories.why: Children killed in the West Bank
sum: Palestinian health officials say Israeli forces killed 14-year-old Moataz Iyad during a raid in Burqa, northwest of Nablus, and are withholding his body. Wafa reported two other young men shot, the boy's father detained and paramedics briefly held. The Israeli military confirmed soldiers opened fire, saying they responded to a threat.

Middle East Eye places the killing in a year of record violence: OCHA logged more than 2,060 settler attacks causing casualties or damage by mid-October, and ACLED says 2026 is the worst year for settler violence since it began monitoring. In Gaza the same day, Israeli fire wounded a fisherman and a boy, per Anadolu.
pts: Boy killed in Burqa raid; Israel holding his body
Army says troops fired at a threat
UN and ACLED record unprecedented settler violence in 2026

stories.h: Providence voters pass divestment and elect a socialist mayor
stories.why: BDS wins at the ballot box
sum: Democracy Now! spoke with David Morales, the 28-year-old democratic socialist just elected mayor of Providence, Rhode Island, where voters also approved Question 7 with over 70% support. The measure orders the city to divest from countries and companies implicated in apartheid, occupation or genocide; it does not name Israel but was driven by the Providence for Palestine Coalition, which gathered over 10,000 signatures after the sitting mayor threatened a veto.

Morales says the city's investment board will now identify holdings to drop. He pledged rent stabilisation and action against ICE. The segment ties the win to other left mayoral victories, including Los Angeles and Washington.
pts: Divestment measure passed with over 70% of the vote
Grassroots petition bypassed a mayoral veto threat
Part of a wider wave of socialist city wins

stories.h: How El-Sayed won Michigan while calling Gaza genocide
sum: Ali Harb examines how Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim US senator, beating Republican Mike Rogers by about seven points in Michigan despite more than $30 million in AIPAC spending against him in the primary and Trump calling him a jihadist. His primary rival endorsed Rogers days before the vote, citing El-Sayed's use of the word genocide; he did not retract it.

El-Sayed linked military aid to Israel and the Iran war to household costs. Harb cites polling showing most Americans now want US aid to Israel cut, and notes Uncommitted co-founder Abbas Alawieh won a state senate seat, while cautioning that a national blue wave also helped.
pts: First Muslim US senator won by about seven points
Survived heavy AIPAC spending and Islamophobic attacks
Writer argues a pro-Palestine stance is now electable
